To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Autodock VINA flexible docking is the method that better discriminates between P-gp ligands and non-ligands, and (ii) the binding affinity of P-gp ligand correlates with the molecular volume of their ligands.

the flexible docking algorithm of Autodock VINA is the best method for predicting the binding affinity of compounds to the human P-glycoproteins, and that this algorithm is able to discriminate between binders and non-binders.
Autodock flexible docking can be used as a filter in virtual screening campaigns to identify compounds that are not substrates for P-gp.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of docking algorithms to the prediction of the affinity of a compound to the P-gp transporter.
the identification of new compounds that are able to bind P-gp and thus to be used as a tool in the design of new drugs.
the identification of new compounds that could be used to reverse the multidrug resistance (MDR) phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Autodock-Vina flexible docking is able to predict with a high degree of confidence the affinity of a compound to the P-gp protein.
Autodock is the best choice to predict P-gp bindin...
docking is a useful approach to predict the interaction of compounds with P-gp, and the results can be used in the rational design and the optimization of new drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
docking can be a useful tool for the prediction of P-gp bindings, and that Autodock is the most reliable program for this task.

we have found that the best conditions to dock P-gp are: flexible ligand docking with the Autodock VINA algorithm, using the 3D structure of the P-gp in the inward-facing conformation (PDB ID 3G60), and using a grid box with a 40 × 30 × 30 Å size.

the docking algorithms are useful to discriminate between binders and non-binders, but only in the case of compounds that are not substrates of P-gp, i.e., that do not bind to P-gp but that are not transported.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of docking to predict P-gp bindability is possible and reliable.
it is possible to use docking to discriminate between binders and nonbinder of P-gp with a high degree of confidence.
docking can be successfully used for the prediction of the affinity of small molecules to P-gp.
